key_insight: A knowledge-guided training strategy can make a neural-network interatomic potential accurate for reactive energetic materials while using far fewer configurations than conventional data-hungry approaches.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable molecular simulation of pyrolysis and shock response in energetic materials, supporting safer materials design and screening.
method: Enhance NNAP with sphmulti: refined spherical-harmonic basis, extra radial basis, and element-specific chemical weighting.
Combine hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria to prioritize informative configurations.
Inject knowledge-guided key events so the model preserves critical reactive pathways during training.
evidence_signal: The NNAP was trained on only 13,680 configurations yet reproduced the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior for 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan.
watch_item: The approach depends on identifying representative key events and sufficient sampling, so performance may drop if rare reactive pathways or loading conditions are missed.
paper_title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
